topic: Hacking with Claude on a $27 Smart Watch: Edge AI Coding Case Study

key_points: Primary source: staff SWE at Strava builds a Casio-style watch face for the $27 PineTime using an AI coding agent in a few hours
PineTime is ideal for AI hacking: cheap ($27), open-source firmware (InfiniTime/any RTOS), well-documented, and has a great simulator (InfiniSim) for a fast feedback loop
Author used OpenCode with open-weights models (Kimi K3 & K2.6, DeepSeek v4 Pro & Flash) — 'Claude' used generically for coding agents
Iterative approach: rough first pass, then fixed one text element at a time with isolated tasks and concrete next steps to save tokens

Key optimization: fullscreen background image for static parts, only program dynamic parts — worked in simulator but pushed hardware limits (10-min BT transfer, 1-2s screen refresh, streams image from filesystem due to RAM limits)
Code pushed to GitHub (mkasberg/InfiniTime/tree/casio) with an AGENTS.md summarizing lessons learned
Low-stakes environment (not production code) enables fast iteration and fun; author had abandoned the watch for 2 years before AI made it approachable
HN discussion (110 points, 20 comments) — community reaction and technical context
Clarification: author actually used OpenCode + open-weights models, not Claude itself — 'Claude' used as generic term (like 'Xerox' or 'ChatGPT')
PineTime has no microphone, so no voice control possible
Hardware constraints discussed: 64KB RAM is a painful bottleneck; original PineTime has 64KB RAM + execute-in-place ROM
Alternative suggestion: Waveshare ESP32-S3 AMOLED 2.09" watch for better display/peripherals/CPU at similar price
PineTime Pro (with more RAM) mentioned as future solution to RAM bottleneck
Official PineTime simulator — gives AI agents a fast feedback loop on the computer without flashing hardware
Has a git submodule for InfiniTime firmware
Author started by cloning this repo and asking Claude to get a build working (quick and easy on Ubuntu)
Open-source firmware for PineTime, community-driven
Runs on numerous RTOSes; the default firmware shipped with PineTime
Well-documented codebase that Claude/AI agents thrive on
Official PineTime specs: 1.3-inch 240x240 IPS capacitive touch display, Nordic nRF52832 64MHz + FPU, Bluetooth 5/BLE, 4MB user storage + 0.5MB OS storage, 180mAh all-week battery, IP67, 38g
Fully open-source, community-driven side project
Ships with InfiniTime firmware, works with Linux/Windows/Android

stats.fact: PineTime costs $27 and runs fully open-source firmware (InfiniTime or any RTOS)
PineTime hardware: 1.3-inch 240x240 IPS touch display, Nordic nRF52832 64MHz + FPU, Bluetooth 5/BLE, 4MB user storage, 0.5MB OS storage, 180mAh battery, IP67, 38g
PineTime has only 64KB of RAM — a painful bottleneck for rendering; the watch streams the fullscreen background image from the filesystem rather than holding it in memory
Transferring a 240x240 fullscreen image over Bluetooth to the PineTime took about 10 minutes; refreshing the whole screen on swipe takes 1-2 seconds
The author built a working custom watch face in a few hours with an AI coding agent — a project he had abandoned for 2 years due to lack of time/motivation to learn the InfiniTime codebase
The HN post reached 110 points with 20 comments, indicating strong community interest in edge-AI coding on cheap hardware

The author used OpenCode with open-weights models (Kimi K3 & K2.6, DeepSeek v4 Pro & Flash) on a limited budget, saving tokens by giving specific feedback with isolated tasks rather than letting the agent run unsupervised

angles: Edge AI coding is democratizing embedded/firmware development — a $27 watch + AI agent replaces months of learning a codebase
The 'Claude' genericization: coding agents (OpenCode, Claude Code, etc.) are becoming the new 'Xerox' — a category, not a brand
Simulator-first workflow (InfiniSim) gives AI agents a fast feedback loop, making hardware hacking approachable without constant flashing
Token-budget pragmatism: letting the human fix one thing at a time beats letting an agent run unsupervised on limited budget
Hardware constraints as creative constraints: fullscreen background image trick to work around 64KB RAM
Low-stakes tinkering as the ideal AI coding sandbox — fun, physical, rewarding, no production risk
The future: PineTime Pro with more RAM, ESP32-S3 alternatives, and voice control (currently impossible — no mic)
